figures.caption: TABLE 4: Best performance of different fusion/detection paradigms vs. our voting mechanism. Bold: best per dataset; underline: second best. All results use the best normalization found in hyperparameter search.

Figure 3: Impact of the voting threshold (Tv) on performance. A threshold of Tv = 4 provides the optimal balance, maximizing the (b) F1 and (c) MCC scores while dramatically reducing the (a) False Positives seen at lower thresholds.

TABLE 1: Attack coverage of PROVFUSION and state-ofthe-art baselines. ✓ denotes a detected campaign (at least one malicious node flagged), while ✗ denotes a miss. PROVFUSION successfully detects 16 out of 17 campaigns. We provide the details of each attack in Appendix D.

Figure 2: The overall architecture of PROVFUSION. It takes raw system logs, prepares a provenance graph, characterizes node anomaly from three complementary views (Attribute, Structural, Causal), and finally fuses these scores to detect anomalies.
